## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Add a new `HydrawiseData` object for caching objects from the API. Use this to refresh the data objects stored in each entity when the coordinator updates.

This fixes a bug where entity states are never updated (since their data is never updated on coordinator refreshes).

issue_context.title: Hydrawise watering sensors stopped working
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The Hydrawise sensors for watering and watering time do not update anymore after the 2023.12 update. Manual control still works.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.12.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2023.11

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Hydrawise

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/hydrawise/

### Diagnostics information

I searched in the diagnostic logs for hydrawise, watering, water, zone names, nothing came up.

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

E.g. sensor.turf_front_watering_time, the sprinklers went off this morning yet the watering time and watering time sensor didn't even get an update. Last time it was updated was 12 hours before the sprinkler went off. It's at a random time that makes no sense and the value stayed 0. I tried reload the integration but nothing worked. It seems to have broke after the 2023.12 update as it was working perfectly before in 2023.11.x.

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

Confirming this is not an isolated problem. Identical issue found, ie the watering wet/dry amd the watering time do not update. Restarting home-assistant fixes the problem of not reflecting the actual watering status, but as you can see it then causes the next cycle data to be invalid. Running core 2023.12.0, but as kirashogun commented, it was happily working in 2023.11.x

The next cycle time is (somewhat) intentional. The API returns a nonsensical value in a few cases (one of which being that the zone is suspended). Previously it was setting a rolling time in the future for this value, which caused the sensor to constantly update. The last release changed it to just set the value to the max datetime. (9999-12-31 23:59:59.999999) While also nonsensical, it's at least stable.

I can fix this to set the value to "Unknown" instead, which I think is more appropriate.
The other issue of the watering status not updating is surprising. I'll look into this.
Ah, I see the problem with data not refreshing. I'll have a PR to fix it shortly.
Thank you so much! :) I'll eagerly await the next release.

review_comments:
As you are the maintainer of the library, can we do it there?

Something like 
```python
class User:
    ...
    controller: dict[int, Controller]
    ...

class Controller:
    ...
    zones: dict[int, Zone]
    ...
```

I'm not sure I agree with this. The purpose of the `HydrawiseData` container is to map the API data in a way that is convenient for HA to consume. For example, I have an upcoming PR that will make additional calls to the API to compute water use by zone. This data is computed and there is no 1-to-1 mapping from the API itself.

The mapping from API data to what is convenient for HA to consume is business logic that does not really belong in the API library. Otherwise, if we have 10 other clients consuming this library, we will end up with 10 different kind of fields for 10 different clients.

Currently, it looks like the library is used only by HA, but the author can give us more insights there.
Looking at the integration code, you only use one zone or controller at a time.
So maybe also the other clients are looping over all zones to find the correct one too. If this will happen then moving the change to the library is reasonable.
If you a client wants still the list, he can always call `.values()`
I'd rather not move this into the library. While the primary reason I wrote the library was for HA, I don't know if there are other users and changing the field type would be a breaking change.

Okay, the change is fine.


One quick notive for the future PRs:
We don't allow device and service integrations to calculate state, and `_async_update_daily_water_use` could do some aggregation in the integration, which is not allowed.
Also, API calls should be made only for enabled entities. For example, I have disabled the flow meter sensor entity in HA, then the coordinator should not make the additional API call.
